title: A Short Overview
text: start, make sure adatutor package installed loaded. use short version altmejd dataset (see R Documentation information). Altmejd et al. (2019) pooled data five large-scale replication projects, use classify replication outcomes social science lab experiment. dataset can loaded :
code: # Load package library(adatutor) #> adatutor: Introducing the Boosting Framework with AdaBoost #> Version: 0.0.1 # Load data data(altmejd)

code: # Stratified split stratsplit <- stratified_split(df, group = "replicate", id = "eid", prop = 0.7) train <- stratsplit$set1 test <- stratsplit$set2

title: A Short Overview
text: AdaBoost algorithm combines multiple base models strong overall model – ensemble. use classification stumps base learners, require following hyperparameter setup:
code: # Tree hyperparameter setup treehypar <- rpart::rpart.control(   # Maximum depth   maxdepth = 1,   # Gini impurity (default)   split = "gini")

title: A Short Overview
text: addition tree hyperparameters, need set boosting hyperparameters. key hyperparameters : T: Number base models eta: Learning rate , develop ensemble 100 stumps learning rate 1:
code: # Boosted stumps and weights fit <- trainAda(replicate ~ ., data = train[, voinms],   # Boosting hyperparameter   T = 10, eta = 1,   # Tree hyperparameter   treehypar = treehypar)

title: A Short Overview
text: model trained, can use make predictions data test set:
code: # Predictions on test set ypred <- testAda(fit, data = test[, prednms])

title: A Short Overview
text: confusion matrix can help us evaluate prediction accuracy:
code: # Confusion matrix table(ypred, test[, outnme]) #>       #> ypred failure success #>    -1      20      11 #>    1        5       9

what: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
title: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
text: function trains set classification trees using AdaBoost. built top rpart package, full range tree hyperparameters can used fine-tune trees (see, e.g., rpart.control). addition, implementation allows customization number trees learning rate. also provides verbose output track training progress.

title: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
code: trainAda(formula, data, T, eta, treehypar, input_checks = TRUE, verbose = TRUE)

title: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
text: formula formula specifying relationship outcome predictors: outcome ~ predictors. predictors included additive terms (e.g., X1 + X2 + ...), Interactions supported (see formula argument rpart). data data frame containing variables model. T integer specifying number trees. eta numeric value representing learning rate algorithm. treehypar list control parameters decision trees (passed rpart.control). input_checks logical value indicating whether perform input validation checks. Defaults TRUE. verbose logical value indicating whether display verbose output training process. Defaults TRUE.

title: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
text: list containing trained weak learners (h) associated weights (). Additional attributes may included model tracking purposes.

title: Train a Set of Classification Trees Using AdaBoost — trainAda
text: function implements AdaBoost algorithm specified number iterations (T). initializes observation weights, trains sequence decision trees, updates weights iteration based prediction errors. final ensemble weak learners produced. Key steps algorithm: Initialize observation weights. Train decision tree using current weights. Compute weighted classification error update observation weights. Store weak learner associated weight.
